title: Dedicated Capacity Governor and Fairness Contract PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD defines the Dedicated Capacity Governor: a policy and control plane that enforces reservation contracts, ensures cross-tenant fairness, and provides deterministic burst behavior for Dedicated customers. The governor sits between the capacity allocator and request router and implements tenant-weighted concurrency limits, contract-aware prewarm budgets, soft-eviction rules, and a tokenized burst allowance. The goal is to reduce noisy-neighbor incidents, deliver predictable latency for paying tenants, and enable safe, auditable burst behavior without manual operator intervention.
background: Customers on Dedicated report two recurring pain points: (1) unpredictable latency during cross-tenant surges, and (2) administrative effort to configure per-tenant burst windows. Existing reserve and autoscale systems handle bulk allocation but lack a declarative enforcement layer that translates contract terms (commit size, priority, burst entitlement) into runtime controls.

Previous PRDs focused on reserve semantics and prewarm heuristics, but did not unify fairness policies or provide an auditable contract-to-runtime translation. This PRD fills that gap with a governor that is policy-driven and observable.

This work pairs Platform (runtime/kernel selection), Orchestration (autoscaler hooks), and Console (policy authoring & telemetry) changes. Engineering dependencies include quota evaluation, token-bucket service, and eviction coordination.
goals: 1) Translate reservation contracts into runtime guards that guarantee baseline concurrency and latency SLOs for committed tenants.
2) Provide a tenant-weighted fairness mechanism for sharing spare capacity during low utilization windows, minimizing tail latency regressions for lower-tier tenants while protecting P0 customers.
3) Implement a safe, auditable burst model with tokenized budgets, decay, and enforcement that can be tuned per-tenant and per-reservation window.
4) Expose clear Console controls and telemetry so PMs and Customer Success can explain behaviors to customers and perform remedial actions.
5) Keep runtime overhead low (<1% P99 path), and provide fallbacks to previous allocation logic if the governor is unhealthy.
non_goals: Full rewrite of the autoscaler logic — autoscaling algorithms remain in scope of separate initiatives.
Replacing customer-level billing or contract negotiation flows; we only enforce agreed terms at runtime.
On-prem air-gapped distribution changes — Private deployables will receive a subset of features in a follow-up.
requirements: REQ-1: Contract ingestion — the governor must consume a machine-readable contract schema describing commit size, priority tier, burst tokens per window, and prewarm allowance.
REQ-2: Baseline reservation enforcement — assigned baseline concurrency and soft-latency SLO must be enforced by rejecting or routing requests to fallback pools when violated.
REQ-3: Tenant-weighted fairness — spare capacity should be allocated proportionally to tenant weight when all baselines are satisfied; weights derive from contract tier + recent historical usage.

REQ-4: Tokenized burst model — each tenant receives burst tokens per defined interval; the governor must decrement tokens on burst usage and prevent burst when depleted; tokens decay with a configurable half-life.
REQ-5: Soft-eviction and graceful degradation — governor must coordinate preemption (best-effort) with minimal disruption and provide metrics + reason codes for evictions.
REQ-6: Observability — emit per-tenant metrics: baseline_satisfied (bool), tokens_remaining, evictions_count, fairness_alloc_pct, decision_trace_id.
REQ-7: Config surface — Console should present a policy editor and simulated evaluation for a tenant contract before applying live.
REQ-8: Health and fallback — if the governor reports errors or high latency, traffic must fall back to pre-governor routing with an alert.
REQ-9: Auditability — every decision that alters request routing (evict, throttle, allow-burst) must be logged with a decision_trace_id persisted for 90 days.
REQ-10: Backwards compatibility — existing customers without contracts continue to operate under current reserved/autoscale behavior (governor defaults to permissive mode).
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I can view per-tenant governor decisions in the Console so I can diagnose latency incidents.
As a Dedicated customer, I want my reservation contract to guarantee a baseline throughput so my latency-sensitive features remain responsive.
As a Customer Success manager, I can simulate a contract change and preview its effect on concurrency and burst behavior before applying it.
As an on-call SRE, I receive an alert when governor fallback occurs and can manually opt to enable degraded-mode routing for affected tenants.
As a product owner, I can define tenant weights to tune fairness allocation across customers in the same pool.
success_metrics: S1: Reduce noisy-neighbor eviction incidents causing P0 latency regressions by 75% in the first 60 days post-release.
S2: 95% of committed tenants see no degradation in P95 latency during typical burst windows compared to baseline.
S3: Governor decision trace logs are available and searchable for 90% of incidents within 10 minutes of occurrence.
S4: Console policy simulator adoption — at least 30% of contract edits use the simulator before commit in the first quarter.
S5: Runtime overhead measured at <1.0% on average request CPU for the P99 path across Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The governor accepts a contract YAML/JSON and creates a policy entry in the Console; policies can be toggled ON/OFF per pool.
AC-2: Under a controlled chaos test (synthetic surge from tenant B while tenant A at baseline), baseline reservations for tenant A are honored in 95% of requests for 30-minute window.
AC-3: Tokenized burst enforcement blocks bursts when tokens are depleted; unit and integration tests validate token decrement and replenishment with configured half-life.
AC-4: Fairness allocation algorithm demonstrates proportional distribution of spare capacity in a simulated multi-tenant scenario; results logged and match expected distribution within 5% variance.
AC-5: All governor decisions generate decision_trace_id and are persisted to the audit log; sample queries across a 7-day window succeed and return the persisted records.
AC-6: If governor health-check fails, traffic falls back to pre-governor routing and an alert is generated; failover verified in chaos-runbook test.
AC-7: Console shows per-tenant telemetry (tokens_remaining, baseline_satisfied, evictions_count) and includes a simulator that predicts outcome for a policy change.
AC-8: No user-facing billing changes occur as a side-effect of governor rollout; billing pipeline validated with test customer accounts.
AC-9: Documentation and runbook published: design doc, operator playbook, and customer-facing FAQ are available prior to release.
AC-10: Security review completed and signed-off; audit log retention and access control validated (role-based visibility).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): Deploy governor in canary pool with two internal test tenants; enable audit-only mode (decisions logged but not enforced) for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (Opt-in Beta): Make policies editable in Console and offer opt-in to 10 pilot customers with small reserves; enforce mode enabled for pilots after 1 week validation.
Phase 2 (Gradual Rollout): Enable governor for 20% of production pools with automatic health monitoring; increment by 20% every week pending SLOs.
Phase 3 (Full): Enable in all Dedicated pools and retire audit-only flags; provide customer communication and support playbook.
Rollback: Toggle policy-level OFF or use node-level governor bypass flag to immediately fallback to prior routing in case of regression.
Communication: Pre-rollout customer emails, Console banner, and a scheduled webinar for enterprise customers explaining the new contract-to-runtime mapping.
monitoring_and_observability: Per-tenant metrics: tokens_remaining, baseline_satisfied(0/1), fairness_alloc_pct, evictions_count, requests_rejected_by_governor.
Logs: decision_trace_id with context (contract_id, tenant_id, pool_id, timestamp, reason_code). Persisted for 90 days.
Dashboards: Dedicated Governor overview, evictions heatmap, fairness allocation per pool.
Alerts: governor_fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, decision_latency_p95 > 200ms, audit-log-write-failures.
Tracing: link decision_trace_id to request traces for end-to-end debugging.
testing_plan: Unit tests for contract ingestion, token accounting, and fairness math.
Integration tests that simulate multi-tenant bursts with varying weights and contract tiers.
Chaos test: simulate governor node crash and validate fallback path and no data loss for decision traces.
Load test: ensure <1% CPU overhead on P99 request path across representative Dedicated hardware profiles.
Security tests: verify RBAC for Console policy editing and audit log access, penetration test of audit-storage path.
migration_plan: Existing reservations without contracts will be ingested with a default permissive contract: tokens=0, weight=1, baseline=existing reservation size.
Bulk migration tool to preview and convert legacy reservations to contract schema; migration runs in read-only mode and outputs CSV for review.
Customers with customized prewarm settings are contacted by Customer Success to confirm contract mapping before enforcement.
Offer an opt-out window of 30 days for customers who need manual configuration before governor enforcement.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (chosen): Tokenized burst + tenant weights — provides predictable, auditable behavior and maps well to contracts but requires extra bookkeeping in the runtime.
Option B: Priority queue preemption — simpler enforcement but can cause poor UX for lower-tier customers and more churn during sustained surges.
Option C: Conservative hard reservations only — easiest to reason about but underutilizes spare capacity and increases cost for customers.
Rationale: Option A balances utilization and predictability while enabling observability and customer-facing controls.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Governor bugs cause widespread latency regressions. Mitigation: progressive rollout with audit-only canary and fast rollback flags.
Risk: Tokens model unintuitive for customers. Mitigation: provide simulator and Customer Success playbook; default conservative token allocation.
Risk: Audit log storage cost. Mitigation: tiered retention (90 days for decision traces, 365 days for policy versions), and sampling for high-volume tenants.
Risk: Cross-service coupling increases operational complexity. Mitigation: clear interface contracts and integration tests between governor, autoscaler, and router.
open_questions: Q1: How should tenant weight be initially derived for customers on legacy contracts? (options: spend-based, commit-size-based, negotiated tier)
Q2: What default half-life for token decay provides the best tradeoff between burst flexibility and cost protection? (suggested: 12 hours)
Q3: Should some enterprise customers be granted unmetered emergency burst tokens under SLA?
Q4: Impact on multi-region routing when a tenant has contracts in multiple regions — should tokens be region-scoped or global?
